question.text:
A lexical analyzer uses the following patterns to recognize three tokens $T_1, T_2$, and $T_3$ over the alphabet $\{x, y, z\}$.

$$
\begin{aligned}
& T_1: x ?(y \mid z)^* y \\
& T_2: y ?(x \mid z)^* x \\
& T_3: z^{+}(x \mid y) ?
\end{aligned}
$$

$y?$ means $0$ or $1$ occurrence of $y$.

The analyzer outputs the token that matches the longest possible prefix. If there is a tie in length, it prioritizes the token with the lowest index $($e.g., $T_1$ over $T_2)$.

If the string $zxxyzyx$ is processed by the analyzer, which one of the following is the sequence of tokens it outputs?
 

  1. $T3,~T2,~T1$
     
  2. $T2, ~T1, ~T2$
     
  3. $T2, ~T1, ~T3$
     
  4. $T1,~T2,~T3$
question.subject: Compiler Design

question.text:
The attributes of three operators in a custom language are given below:
\begin{array}{llll}
\text { OPERATOR } & \text { PRECEDENCE } & \text { ASSOCIATIVITY } & \text { ARITY } \\
\text { # (Square) } & \text { HIGH } & \text { RIGHT } & \text { UNARY (Postfix) } \\
\text { ^ (Power) } & \text { MEDIUM } & \text { RIGHT } & \text { BINARY } \\
+ \text { (Plus) } & \text { LOW } & \text { LEFT } & \text { BINARY }
\end{array}


OPERATOR DEFINITIONS:

  • $\mathbf{x \#}=x^2$ (Square the number before it)
     
  • $\mathbf{x}^{\wedge} \mathbf{y}=x^y$ (Standard power)
     
  • $\mathbf{x + y}=x+y$ (Standard addition)
     

Evaluate the following expression:

$$
5+2 ~^{\wedge} ~2 ~\#  ~^{\wedge}~ 2
$$
question.subject: Compiler Design

question.text:
The attributes of three symbolic operators are given below:

\[
\begin{array}{llll}
\text{OPERATOR} & \text{PRECEDENCE} & \text{ASSOCIATIVITY} & \text{ARITY} \\
\& & \text{HIGH} & \textbf{RIGHT} & \text{Binary} \\
1 & \text{MEDIUM} & \text{LEFT} & \text{Binary} \\
\Longrightarrow & \text{LOW} & \text{LEFT} & \text{Binary}
\end{array}
\]


Rules for this language:

  • $A \& B$ is defined as $(A \times B)$
     
  • $A \| B$ is defined as $(A+B)$
     
  • $A \Longrightarrow B$ is defined as $(A-B)$
     

The value of the expression $10 \Longrightarrow 2 ~\&~ 3 ~\&~ 2 ~\|~ 5$ in this language is $\_\_\_\_$ .
question.subject: Compiler Design

question.text:
Consider the following augmented grammar with $\{+, *,(),, i d\}$ as the set of terminals.

$$
\begin{aligned}
& T^{\prime} \rightarrow T \\
& T \rightarrow T+F \\
& T \rightarrow F \\
& F \rightarrow F * P \\
& F \rightarrow P \\
& P \rightarrow(T) \\
& P \rightarrow i d
\end{aligned}
$$

Let $I_0=\operatorname{CLOSURE}\left(\left\{T^{\prime} \rightarrow \bullet T\right\}\right)$.

The number of items in the set $\operatorname{GOTO}\left(\operatorname{GOTO}\left(I_0, F\right), *\right)$ is $\_\_\_\_$ .
question.subject: Compiler Design

question.text:
Consider the following augmented grammar with $\{+, \uparrow, a, b\}$ as the set of terminals. Note that $\epsilon$ represents the empty string.

$$
\begin{aligned}
& S^{\prime} \rightarrow S \\
& S \rightarrow A+S \\
& S \rightarrow b \\
& A \rightarrow a A \uparrow \\
& A \rightarrow \epsilon
\end{aligned}
$$

Let $I_0=\operatorname{CLOSURE}\left(\left\{S^{\prime} \rightarrow \bullet S\right\}\right)$.

The number of items in the set $\operatorname{GOTO}\left(I_0, a\right)$ is $\_\_\_\_$ .
question.subject: Compiler Design
